essence: Kaumārī mind-formed offers distinction-flowers from the south: thoughts themselves the gift.
Vaiṣṇavī hearing-formed offers sound-flowers from the southwest: listening itself the rite.
Vārāhī skin-formed delights with touch-flowers from the west: feeling itself pleasing.
Indrāṇī sight-bodied honors with choicer forms from the northwest: seeing itself worship.
Cāmuṇḍā tongue-called honors with six-taste foods from the north: tasting itself offered.
Mahālakṣmī nose-called worshipped with perfumes from the northeast: smelling itself the rite; circle complete.
Kṣetrapati self-named, 36-reality-infused, worshipped in six views: the experiencer guards the field.
The quivering experience-pith ever near: one's own god-circle hymned as first-person presence.

rasa.dominant: adbhuta settling toward śānta (wonder circling home to rest)
rasa.justification: Six sense-offerings complete the round and the field-lord gathers them into one experiencer; the round rests the wonder it built. Praise that began in beholding ends in belonging.

sections.SUMMARY: Kaumārī mind-formed with distinction-flowers from the south: thoughts offered. Vaiṣṇavī hearing-formed with sound-flowers from the southwest: listening laid down. Vārāhī skin-formed delighting with touch-flowers from the west. Indrāṇī sight-bodied honoring with choicer forms from the northwest. Cāmuṇḍā tongue-called honoring with six-taste foods from the north. Mahālakṣmī nose-called worshipped with perfumes from the northeast: the circle stands complete. Kṣetrapati self-named, thirty-six-reality-infused, worshipable in six views, giver of siddhis. The quivering pith of experience ever near: my own body's god-circle hymned.
sections.FUNCTION: Completes the offerings sense by sense, gathers them into the field's one experiencer, and rests the round in first-person presence.
sections.KEY TERMS: kusuma-pattern (each sense offers its own flowers — resolve, distinction, sound, touch, forms, tastes, perfumes); manas/śruti/tvac/dṛk/jihvā/ghrāṇa (six sense-powers as goddesses); kṣetrapati (field-lord as first-person experiencer); ṣaṭtriṃśattattva (thirty-six as the full map); ṣaḍdarśana (six views as unanimous witness); viśeṣa (distinction — edition text, vikalpa variant recorded); śabda (sound — edition text, śabdarūpā variant recorded).
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: Six petals yet to give; the field-lord gathers the many offerers into one experiencer; beholding turns to belonging.
sections.BOUNDARY: Distinction-flowers and sound-flowers stand as offered; the thoughts-reading and the sound-formed reading wait aside. The count of tattvas and views is stated, never derived.
sections.EXPLANATION: Each remaining sense brings its own flowers: thoughts from mind in the south, sounds from hearing in the southwest, touch from skin in the west, forms from sight in the northwest, tastes from tongue in the north, perfumes from smell in the northeast. Nothing in the body is rejected; every sense becomes an offerer. Then the field itself gets its lord: worshipable wherever looked for, infused with all thirty-six realities, self-named, giving powers. Quivering experience, within all, ever near — one's own circle, hymned as oneself.
sections.RELATED: Dyczkowski per-verse exposition (petal-direction mapping, Kṣetrapati as first-person experiencer); print variants v9 (vikalpa) and v10 (śabdarūpā) flagged in argmaps; Sharada ms (Jammu No 67) different opening — transmission noted, not collated.
